subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219's derived longer isolated-cron setup watchdog, require a different cap/config policy, or keep the current 60s fail-fast behavior?
rationale: The source fix is narrow, but it changes the default availability tradeoff for stuck runner setup and the repository policy treats config/default and fallback behavior as maintainer-sensitive.

options.title: Accept bounded longer setup window
options.body: Merge the current open PR or equivalent if maintainers accept that isolated cron setup may occupy a cron slot longer before timing out.

options.title: Tighten or configure the cap
options.body: Ask for a lower cap or explicit operator-tunable policy before merge if cron-slot occupancy is more important than busy-host cold-start tolerance.

options.title: Keep fail-fast behavior
options.body: Reject longer setup windows and close or retarget the issue only if maintainers decide the 60s cap is intentional product behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded longer setup window
recommendation.body: Merge the current open PR or equivalent if maintainers accept that isolated cron setup may occupy a cron slot longer before timing out.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron watchdog owner boundaries and product/default tradeoffs, and this person appears in the relevant cron timer refactor history.
